THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING ON I.A., THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant, seeking enhancement of the compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case are that on 08.07.2014, at about 4.00 p.m., the claimant was going on footpath road, near Thimmarayaswamy Arch, Anekal- Hosur Road, Anekal Town, Bangalore, at that time, all of a sudden, the rider of the Honda Scooter bearing registration No.KA-51-EJ-1553 ridden in high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the claimant.
Due to the impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Therefore, the claimant has filed the claim petition,
seeking compensation.

3. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for the respondent- Insurance Company and perused the records.
4.

The Tribunal after considering the facts and circumstances and evidence on record, has awarded compensation of Rs.2,42,491/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of Ashwathappa vs Bharathi Axa General Insurance Co. Ltd on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14054365/
2 petition till the date of realization, under the following heads:
SL.NO. PARTICULARS AMOUNT  (IN.RS.)
 1. Pain and sufferings 50,000-00

Future medical expenses 10,000-00  Total 2,42,491-00 5.
Being aggrieved by the lesser quantum of compensation, the present appeal is filed.
6. In the present case, the claimant was aged about 65 years at the time of accident, working as a security guard and earning Rs.7,500/- per month.
The medical records proves that the claimant has suffered fracture of shaft of right femur, fracture of shaft of left humerus, which are grievous in nature.
He took treatment in Sanjay Gandhi Hospital for 42 days as an in-patient.
PW2-doctor has stated that the appellant/claimant has suffered 17% of permanent partial disability to the right lower limb and 6% of disability towards left upper limb.
But, the doctor has not stated about disability towards whole body.

Therefore, looking to the injuries suffered and permanent partial disability to the right lower limb suffered by the claimant, the Tribunal has taken the disability to the whole body as 11%, which is on the lesser side.
Therefore, the compensation awarded under each head is to be modified.

7. The Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.50,000/- under the head 'Pain and sufferings',
which is on the lesser side and the same is enhanced to Rs.60,000/-.
8.
The compensation of Rs.53,959/- awarded under the head 'Medical Expenses' is as per the bills produced by the claimant.
The same is kept in tact.
9. The claimant has taken treatment in the hospital as an in-patient for about 42 days.
He must not have attended the work at least for a period of 6 months.

Therefore, a sum of Rs.51,000/-
(Rs.8,500x 6 months) is awarded under the head 'Loss of income during laid up period'.

10. PW2-doctor has stated that the claimant has suffered 6% disability to the left upper limb and 17% of disability to the right lower limb, in total the claimant has suffered 23% of permanent partial disability to the limb.
It is stated that the claimant is unable to work of security guard due to the injuries as well as the disability suffered by him.

The Tribunal has erred in taking the disability to Ashwathappa vs Bharathi Axa General Insurance Co. Ltd on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14054365/
3 the whole body as 11%.

sentences.text: The claimant has suffered fracture of left leg femur and fracture of left hand.

Therefore, looking to the injuries, fracture suffered and difficulties faced by the claimant as stated by the doctor, it is just and proper to consider the permanent partial disability to the whole body as 23%.
The claimant was aged about 65 years at the time of accident.
The notional income of the claimant is to be taken at Rs.8,500/- per month as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authorities.
The appropriate multiplier applicable is '7'.
Therefore, 'loss of earning capacity due to disability' is re-
assessed and quantified as Rs.1,64,220/- (Rs.8,500x23%x7x12).
11. The compensation of Rs.20,000/- awarded by the Tribunal under the head 'Loss of Amenities' is on the lesser side.
The same is enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.
12. The compensation of Rs.20,000/- awarded under the head 'Conveyance, nourishment, food and attendant charges' is on the lesser side.
The claimant has taken treatment in the hospital about 42 days as an in-patient.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.50,000/- under the said head.
13. The Tribunal has awarded a lesser sum of Rs.10,000/- under the head 'Future Medical Expenses'.
The same is enhanced to Rs.35,000/-.

14. Thus, in all, the claimant is entitled for the following compensation :
 SL.NO. PARTICULARS AMOUNT  (IN.RS.)
 1. Pain and sufferings 60,000-00
2 . Conveyance, nourishment, 50,000-00  food and attendant charges  3.
Medical expenses 53,959-00  4. Loss of future income due to 1,64,220-00  disability
5. Loss of income during laid up 51,000-00  period  6. Loss of amenities 50,000-00  7.
Future medical expenses 35,000-00  Total 4,64,179-00 15.
The Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.2,42,491/- but the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.4,64,179/-.

Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.2,21,688/- (Rs.4,64,179 - Rs.2,42,491) along with interest @ 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till its realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

16. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
